video.title: Forget Dropshipping. Be The Middleman For $800+/Job (Drop-Servicing)

summary: Chris Koerner tours a concrete-leveling (polyurethane foam lifting) operation in Houston with Jeff, a W-2 employee and father who started 90 days earlier and subcontracts all the physical work. Jeff claims almost $20k revenue, 30-40% gross margins and a $2,500 average job. He gets leads via Facebook ads, Nextdoor, Google, referrals, a Replit-built site with chatbots and HighLevel texting, and quotes jobs remotely from photos. Koerner shows the maths that about 36 leads a month and about 5 quoting hours a week could yield $10k/month profit. Key takeaway: a drop-servicing model, where you sell, quote and coordinate while insured subcontractors do the work, can run part-time, though the claims are early-stage and self-reported.

speakers.name: Jeff
speakers.description: W-2 employee and father running a Houston concrete leveling drop-servicing business (texaslabguys.com), 90 days in

ideas.name: Concrete leveling drop-servicing (subcontracted foam lifting)
ideas.one_liner: Sell and quote concrete leveling jobs to homeowners and commercial owners, subcontract the work to trailer-owning operators and keep a 30-40% margin.
ideas.business_model: Per-job fee; markup over subcontractor cost; 50% deposit, balance on completion
ideas.customer: Homeowners (trip hazards, aesthetics, avoiding replacement); also HOA managers, property managers, new home builders and retail property owners
ideas.problem: Sunken or uneven concrete slabs (sidewalks, driveways, parking lots) are trip hazards and ugly; replacement costs roughly 10x more
ideas.offer: Polyurethane foam concrete leveling at about a third of the cost of new concrete, with a quality guarantee, excellent communication and a free power wash on residential jobs

pricing.model: Quote per job based on estimated foam volume; minimum project around $1,000

price_points.label: minimum small job quote when subbing
cost of subcontractor on a small job

pricing.notes: Avoids bidding wars; because he subs out he is more expensive than owner-operators and may close fewer jobs. Conservative foam estimates are built into quotes. Travel time must be factored in (first job at an hour outside town earned no margin).

acquisition_channels.details: Facebook ad campaign; first lead within 1-2 hours of launch at about $4.60 per lead, converting to a $2,500 job; turns campaigns on and off

quote.text: My cost per lead was, you know, $4.60 or something, and I found that lead within an hour or two of the campaign being approved and launched.
quote.speaker: Jeff

acquisition_channels.details: Google search organic plus inbound website leads captured by forms and chatbots
Outbound texting campaigns thanking HOA managers and property managers who oversee multiple properties; slow trickle of volume. UK PECR would restrict this for individuals and sole traders.

ideas.delivery: Insured subcontractors with their own foam-lifting trailers do the work. Jeff quotes remotely from photos and phone calls, books jobs never in the same week, takes a 50% deposit, and requires subs to send photos and check-ins. A power washer subbed out 2-3 days later is baked into the quote and upsold for backyards at $100.
unit_economics_claims: Almost $20k revenue in 90 days, mostly in the last 60
Small job: sub costs $600-700, charge at least $1,000
Close rate about 33% on qualified quotes
Own-equipment entry about $120k for a 20ft trailer, or $60-70k for a van
ideas.startup_cost: Near zero when subcontracting: CRM plus Replit under about $500-600/month; website built at $0. Owning equipment would cost $60-70k (van) to $120k (20ft trailer).
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: First job sold June 2025, about 2 hours after launching the Facebook campaign; roughly 90 days to almost $20k revenue.

acquisition.how: Paid Facebook ads, SEO, a landing page and chatbots can run with agents. Nextdoor organic and the outbound texting are weaker and PECR-restricted in the UK.

onboarding.how: HighLevel automations text new leads instantly, a chatbot qualifies them and photos are collected remotely; agents can draft quotes, but a human or phone call still helps close.

delivery.how: Physical foam lifting by subcontractors. Dispatch, scheduling and photo check-ins can be tooled, but a human must find, vet and manage subs and estimate foam volumes.

billing.how: 50% deposit and balance on completion can be invoiced and chased by software with light approval.

support.how: Chatbots and automated texts handle inquiries and updates; disputes and on-site problems need a human.

uk_applicability.notes: The model of selling and subcontracting a trade works anywhere, but UK concrete is mostly poured on lower-volume sites and has less slab settling than Texas. Foam lifting exists in the UK, but the market is smaller, and PECR limits outbound texting. A UK version would need subcontractors with public liability insurance and a different demand profile.

risks: Unexpected voids can multiply costs (a $1,500 job became $5,000)
Under-estimating foam is the quickest way to lose money
Subcontractor quality or reliability, since the business depends entirely on subs
Higher price than owner-operators lowers close rate
Remote quoting lowers win rate to about 25%
Saturated markets; a large owned-equipment path requires heavy capex
Results are only 90 days old and self-reported

tactics.name: Fast Facebook lead ads plus instant text follow-up
steps: Launch a Facebook ad campaign for the service and area
Use HighLevel to text each lead right after the form is submitted
Ask if they are free to connect, then call regardless of reply
Respond to leads immediately with no downtime

quote.text: it goes a long way if you get a text right after you complete a form, and then ask if they're free to connect, and then call them regardless of what they say.
quote.speaker: Jeff

tactics.name: Remote photo-based quoting
steps: Ask for photographs instead of driving to site
Ask educated questions about trees, water lines and sprinklers
Quote conservatively on foam volume
Accept a lower win rate (about 25%) in exchange for 5-10 quotes in the time of one site visit

quote.text: I can crank out five or 10 quotes, you know, the time it takes me to drive an hour outside of town
quote.speaker: Jeff

tactics.name: Free power wash differentiator baked into price
steps: Include a free power wash in the quote for residential jobs
Sub out the power wash 2-3 days after leveling for about $100-150
Text the owner offering sidewalks free and a backyard for $100
Use the upsell to cover the cost

quote.text: you level your driveway with us, we'll power wash your driveway for free.
quote.speaker: Jeff

tactics.name: Subcontractor control and deposit terms
steps: Never book jobs in the same week
Take 50% deposit on sale and the rest on completion
Require subs to hold $1-2M insurance
Require pictures and check-ins and a firm arrival time

quote.text: each sub has to have at least a million dollars of insurance, one to two million dollars

tactics.name: Recruit plateaued solo operators

warnings.warning: Avoid bidding wars; those customers tend to be more of a pain over time.
Rolling a truck for a small job strains margin after fuel and travel time.

lessons.lesson: Selling and coordinating a trade service while subcontracting the physical work lets someone with a full-time job run it, since the owner's work is leads, quotes and subcontractor oversight.
Fast lead response (text immediately, then call) is a cheap competitive edge in local services.
Trading a lower win rate for much higher quote volume can increase total revenue; test the maths.
Differentiate on communication and guaranteed quality, not price, to avoid bidding wars.
Bake small freebies, like a power wash, into the quote so they raise perceived value for little cost.
Back-solve profit targets into leads, quotes and hours before committing.
Choose a validated, old industry and bring modern marketing and systems rather than inventing a new market.

quote.text: choose a service or a line of work that has already been validated for centuries
quote.speaker: Jeff

lessons.lesson: Recurring contracts increase revenue predictability and justify buying assets.
Make subcontractors carry their own insurance and prove work with photos and check-ins to protect yourself.
Selling the problem (liability, pain) works better than selling aesthetics in B2B.

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand operator with specific numbers (revenue, margins, CPL, close rate), but only 90 days of history, figures are self-reported and cannot be verified, and growth targets are aspirational. Koerner's $10k/month maths is hypothetical.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Koerner promotes his paid community tkowners.com; Jeff promotes texaslabguys.com and seeks commercial real-estate connections.
